+body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0; background: var(--bg); color: var(--text); }
+.top { background: var(--header-bg); color: var(--header-text); padding: 1rem 2rem; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1rem; flex-wrap: wrap; }
main { max-width: 640px; margin: 2rem auto; display: grid; gap: 1.5rem; }
-.card { background: white; border-radius: 8px; padding: 1.25rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); }
+.card { background: var(--card-bg); border-radius: 8px; padding: 1.25rem; box-shadow: var(--card-shadow); }
form label { display: block; margin-top: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; }
-.help-icon { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 1.2em; height: 1.2em; border-radius: 50%; background: #e5e7eb; font-size: 0.8em; cursor: help; }
+form input { width: 100%; padding: 0.5rem; box-sizing: border-box; background: var(--input-bg); color: var(--text); border: 1px solid var(--input-border); border-radius: 4px; }
+.help-icon { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 1.2em; height: 1.2em; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--help-bg); font-size: 0.8em; cursor: help; }
-#task-list li { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; padding: 0.5rem 0; border-bottom: 1px solid #eee; }
+#task-list li { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; padding: 0.5rem 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); }
+/* Theme toggle (segmented control in the header) */
+.theme-toggle { display: inline-flex; border: 0; margin: 0; padding: 2px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--toggle-bg); }
+.theme-toggle legend { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; }
+.theme-toggle button { font: inherit; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 0.3rem 0.8rem; border: 0; border-radius: 999px; background: transparent; color: var(--header-text); }
+.theme-toggle button[aria-pressed="true"] { background: var(--toggle-active-bg); color: var(--toggle-active-text); font-weight: 600; }

content.text:
I added a dark theme to the three existing files. The page follows the OS setting by default, and a Light / Dark / System switch in the header lets the user override it. I haven't opened it in a browser, and the JavaScript syntax check didn't run because it needed your approval, so this is untested.

- **`style.css`**: all the hard-coded colours are now theme variables, with a light set and a dark set. Dark is used when the OS prefers dark (unless the user picked Light), or when the user explicitly picked Dark. Form inputs, the help icon, the red invalid-field state, list dividers and card shadows all get dark versions. The header is now a flex row, with the title on the left and the switch on the right.
- **`index.html`**:
  - The header has the three-button switch. Each button reports whether it's selected, so screen readers announce the current choice.
  - A small script at the top of the page applies the saved choice before anything is drawn, so the page doesn't flash in the wrong theme on load.
  - A tag tells the browser the page supports both light and dark, so scrollbars and built-in controls like the date picker match.
- **`app.js`**: clicking Light or Dark saves the choice in the browser and applies it straight away. Clicking System deletes the saved choice and goes back to following the OS, including live changes to the OS setting. If the browser blocks storage (for example in private browsing), the switch still works for that visit but won't be remembered.

To check it, open `index.html`, try each option, reload to confirm the choice sticks, and with System selected change your OS appearance to see the page follow it.
